sentences.en: Hi, I'm Andrew Ross-Sorkin.
sentences.zh: 嗨，我是安德鲁·罗斯·索尔金。

sentences.en: I cover business and policy for DealBook, a daily newsletter at The New York Times.
sentences.zh: 我是《纽约时报》每日简报 DealBook 的商业与政策记者。

sentences.en: On November 18th, I'm going to be interviewing some of the most consequential leaders in business, politics, and culture, including J.D.
sentences.zh: 11月18日，我将在纽约市 DealBook 峰会的现场，采访商界、政界和文化界最具影响力的领袖，包括 J.D.

sentences.en: Vance, Elon Musk, Christine Lagarde,
sentences.zh: 万斯、埃隆·马斯克、克里斯蒂娜·拉加德、

sentences.en: Zylran Mondani, and many others, live on stage at the DealBook Summit in New York City.
sentences.zh: 齐尔兰·蒙达尼以及许多其他人。

sentences.en: You can watch some of these unguarded, unfiltered conversations as they happen.
sentences.zh: 您可以实时观看其中一些毫无防备、未经过滤的对话。

sentences.en: We're going to be live-streaming select interviews for anyone to watch, free, at nytimes.com on November 18th.
sentences.zh: 11月18日，我们将在 nytimes.com 上免费直播部分精选访谈，供任何人观看。

sentences.en: If you're not already a subscriber, you can download the New York Times app to watch and get a month of free access to all of our journalism.
sentences.zh: 如果您还不是订阅者，可以下载《纽约时报》应用程序进行观看，并获得我们所有新闻内容的一个月免费访问权限。

sentences.en: I hope you'll tune in.
sentences.zh: 希望您能收看。

sentences.en: You won't want to miss it.
sentences.zh: 您一定不想错过。

sentences.en: From the New York Times, I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是来自《纽约时报》的迈克尔·巴巴罗。

sentences.en: This is The Deal.
sentences.zh: 这里是《交易》。

sentences.en: Today.
sentences.zh: 今天。

sentences.en: In 2013, Abigail Fisher sued the University of Texas, saying she was discriminated against for being white.
sentences.zh: 2013年，阿比盖尔·费雪起诉德克萨斯大学，称她因白人身份而受到歧视。

sentences.en: Now, a group of students are suing Harvard, saying they were discriminated against for being Asian American.
sentences.zh: 如今，一群学生正在起诉哈佛大学，称他们因身为亚裔美国人而受到歧视。

sentences.en: Both lawsuits take aim at affirmative action, and both can be traced to the same man.
sentences.zh: 这两起诉讼都将矛头指向平权法案，并且都可以追溯到同一个人。

sentences.en: But this time, the White House is taking up his cause.
sentences.zh: 但这一次，白宫正在支持他的诉求。

sentences.en: It's Friday, August 4th.
sentences.zh: 今天是8月4日，星期五。

sentences.en: Brief background, I guess.
sentences.zh: 我想先简单介绍一下背景。

sentences.en: So I had, I think it was a 4.67, if I remember correctly, for my GPA.
sentences.zh: 如果我没记错的话，我的 GPA 大概是 4.67。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: So you had, you had, you had more than a 4.0.
sentences.zh: 所以你的 GPA 超过了 4.0。

sentences.en: Yeah, I had more than a 4.0.
sentences.zh: 对，我的 GPA 超过了 4.0。

sentences.en: I took multiple honors in AP classes.
sentences.zh: 我修了多门荣誉课程和大学先修课程（AP）。

sentences.en: Got it.
sentences.zh: 明白了。

sentences.en: I had a perfect ACT score.
sentences.zh: 我的 ACT 考试取得了满分。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: For extracurriculars, I played the piano for over 15 years.
sentences.zh: 在课外活动方面，我弹了15年以上的钢琴。

sentences.en: I did speech and debate.
sentences.zh: 我参加了演讲和辩论。

sentences.en: I also sang in a choir, which actually went to Obama's inauguration back in 08.
sentences.zh: 我还加入了一个合唱团，该合唱团实际上在08年参加了奥巴马的就职典礼。

sentences.en: You sang at, you sang at Barack Obama's inauguration for president?
sentences.zh: 你在贝拉克·奥巴马的总统就职典礼上唱歌？

sentences.en: Yep, his first inauguration, that's correct.
sentences.zh: 是的，他的第一次就职典礼，没错。

sentences.en: This keeps getting better.
sentences.zh: 这真是越来越厉害了。

sentences.en: There's a lot of stuff.
sentences.zh: 还有很多事情。

sentences.en: I think that mostly summarizes it.
sentences.zh: 我想这基本上就概括了。

sentences.en: So, with that resume, where did you apply to college?
sentences.zh: 那么，带着这样的简历，你申请了哪些大学？

sentences.en: I applied to all Ivey's except one.
sentences.zh: 除了常春藤盟校中的一所，我都申请了。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: And how many accepted you?
sentences.zh: 有多少学校录用了你？

sentences.en: One.
sentences.zh: 一所。

sentences.en: That was 10.
sentences.zh: 那是10号。

sentences.en: What was your reaction to that ratio of acceptance to rejection?
sentences.zh: 你对录取与拒绝的比例有什么反应？

sentences.en: I was definitely quite disappointed in that.
sentences.zh: 我对此绝对相当失望。

sentences.en: So, I actually reached out to the school's admissions offices.
sentences.zh: 所以，我实际上联系了学校的招生办公室。

sentences.en: I wanted to know how these schools used race as a factor of consideration.
sentences.zh: 我想知道这些学校是如何将种族作为考量因素的。

sentences.en: So, I was wondering whether my race had any factor or how large a proportion did it play?
sentences.zh: 所以，我在想我的种族是否起了什么作用，或者它占了多大的比例？

sentences.en: You know, there's just a natural perception that there's a quota set on how many Asian-American students a school can accept.
sentences.zh: 你知道，人们自然会有一种看法，认为学校对可以招收多少亚裔美国学生设有配额。

sentences.en: Because there are so many qualified Asian-American students that it would be difficult to accept them all.
sentences.zh: 因为有太多合格的亚裔美国学生，要把他们全部录取是很困难的。

sentences.en: So, they're going to have to turn away some.
sentences.zh: 所以，他们不得不拒绝一些人。

sentences.en: There just seems to be, like, a separate standard except for Asian-Americans in which their minimum bar is set higher than that of other races.
sentences.zh: 似乎存在着一种针对亚裔美国人的独立标准，他们的最低门槛比其他种族定得更高。

sentences.en: I wanted to see if there was any evidence or any kind of signs showing that.
sentences.zh: 我想看看是否有任何证据或任何迹象表明这一点。

sentences.en: And tell me about Harvard in particular.
sentences.zh: 跟我说说哈佛大学的具体情况。

sentences.en: Is that where you were most eager to go?
sentences.zh: 那是你最渴望去的学校吗？

sentences.en: Yale and Harvard was pretty much a tie for me.
sentences.zh: 耶鲁和哈佛对我的吸引力差不多。

sentences.en: If I had offers from both schools, it would be quite a tough decision to choose which one.
sentences.zh: 如果我同时收到这两所学校的录用通知，选择去哪一所将是一个非常艰难的决定。

sentences.en: Both schools are equally as good.
sentences.zh: 两所学校一样好。

sentences.en: So, it would be hard to choose between one of those two.
sentences.zh: 所以，在这两所学校之间做出选择会很困难。

sentences.en: But definitely, those were among my top two schools I really wanted to go.
sentences.zh: 但毫无疑问，这两所是我最想去的顶尖学校之一。

sentences.en: After the rejection from Harvard, Michael Wang joined a group of Asian-American students who questioned the university's decision-making process.
sentences.zh: 在遭到哈佛大学拒绝后，迈克尔·王加入了一群质疑该校决策过程的亚裔美国学生。

sentences.en: My colleague, Anna Mona Hartakalas, is reporting on the story.
sentences.zh: 我的同事安娜·莫娜·哈塔卡拉斯正在报道这个故事。

sentences.en: So, in November of 2014, a group calling itself Students for Fair Admissions filed a lawsuit in federal court in Boston against Harvard University,
sentences.zh: 因此，在2014年11月，一个自称为“公平招生学生”的组织在波士顿的联邦法院对哈佛大学提起了诉讼，

sentences.en: alleging discrimination and admissions against Asian-Americans.
sentences.zh: 指控其在招生中对亚裔美国人存在歧视。

sentences.en: And the lawsuit says that Harvard has been doing this through what are essentially illegal quotas.
sentences.zh: 诉讼称，哈佛大学一直通过本质上非法的配额来做到这一点。

sentences.en: And the Supreme Court has ruled that numeric quotas are not acceptable in college admissions.
sentences.zh: 最高法院已经裁定，数字配额在大学招生中是不可接受的。

sentences.en: Harvard says it doesn't have them.
sentences.zh: 哈佛表示它没有这种配额。

sentences.en: But this lawsuit says that, in effect, it does.
sentences.zh: 但这起诉讼称，实际上它确实有。

sentences.en: Because year after year after year, roughly the same percentage of Asians and of whites and of blacks, of Hispanics, are admitted to the freshman class.
sentences.zh: 因为年复一年，大约相同比例的亚裔、白人、黑人和西班牙裔被录用为新生。

sentences.en: So, they're saying if Harvard were going strictly on merit, there would be a lot more Asian-American students there.
sentences.zh: 所以，他们说如果哈佛完全按成绩录取，那里会有更多的亚裔美国学生。

sentences.en: And Harvard doesn't want that because that would reduce the numbers of white students and black students and Hispanic students.
sentences.zh: 哈佛不希望这样，因为那会减少白人学生、黑人学生和西班牙裔学生的人数。

sentences.en: And what's happening with this legal case now?
sentences.zh: 这个法律案件现在进展如何？

sentences.en: So, just a few months after the lawsuit was filed, a coalition of 64 Asian-American groups went to the Department of Justice
sentences.zh: 因此，在诉讼提起几个月后，一个由64个亚裔美国人团体组成的联盟前往司法部，

sentences.en: and actually the Education Department as well to file a complaint that tracks very close to the lawsuit.
sentences.zh: 实际上还有教育部，提出了与诉讼非常接近的投诉。

sentences.en: And this was under the Obama administration.
sentences.zh: 这是在奥巴马政府时期发生的。

sentences.en: It sort of languished in the Justice Department.
sentences.zh: 它在司法部有点被搁置了。

sentences.en: Now a new administration has come in.
sentences.zh: 现在新政府上台了。

sentences.en: And they say that they're going to look at it.
sentences.zh: 他们表示将对此进行调查。

sentences.en: So, the Trump administration took a case that the Obama administration basically ignored and said, we are going to do something about this.
sentences.zh: 因此，特朗普政府接手了一个被奥巴马政府基本忽视的案件，并表示我们要对此采取行动。

sentences.en: Correct.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And what are they doing about it?
sentences.zh: 他们正在采取什么行动？

sentences.en: So, the Department of Justice posted a job opening for lawyers who would work on university admissions discrimination.
sentences.zh: 司法部发布了一个职位空缺，招聘专门负责大学招生歧视案的律师。

sentences.en: Essentially, affirmative action is what we're talking about.
sentences.zh: 本质上，我们谈论的就是平权法案。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对的。

sentences.en: So, they're taking up the issue of affirmative action.
sentences.zh: 所以，他们正在处理平权法案的问题。

sentences.en: Based on this lawsuit, give me a sense of what it's like for Asian-Americans applying to college right now.
sentences.zh: 根据这起诉讼，让我大致了解一下目前亚裔美国人申请大学的情况。

sentences.en: All right.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: So, the lawsuit actually likens it.
sentences.zh: 诉讼实际上将其进行了类比。

sentences.en: I think this is an interesting point to discrimination against Jews at Harvard going back to the 1910s, 20s, 30s,
sentences.zh: 我认为这是一个有趣的观点，即针对20世纪10年代、20年代、30年代哈佛大学对犹太人的歧视，

sentences.en: when many historians have said there was an informal quota against Jews who were then the high-achieving minority and started to get too numerous at Harvard.
sentences.zh: 当时许多历史学家表示，存在针对犹太人的非正式配额，他们当时是高成就的少数群体，并开始在哈佛变得人数过多。

sentences.en: So, now the lawsuit claims the same thing is happening with Asians.
sentences.zh: 因此，现在诉讼声称同样的事情正在亚裔身上发生。

sentences.en: They're the high-achieving minority and they're being penalized for it.
sentences.zh: 他们是高成就的少数群体，却因此受到惩罚。

sentences.en: So, some research has shown, for instance, that to get into a school like Harvard as an Asian-American,
sentences.zh: 例如，一些研究表明，作为一个亚裔美国人要考入像哈佛这样的学校，

sentences.en: you need to have an SAT score that's 140 points higher than a white applicant.
sentences.zh: 你的 SAT 分数需要比白人申请者高出 140 分。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So, in the lawsuit, it quotes the Princeton Review, which is a very mainstream college prep company.
sentences.zh: 因此，诉讼中引用了普林斯顿评论，这是一个非常主流的大学预科公司。

sentences.en: If you are an Asian-American, or even if you simply have an Asian or Asian-sounding surname, you need to be careful about what you do and don't say in your application.
sentences.zh: 如果你是一名亚裔美国人，或者即使你只是有一个亚裔或听起来像亚裔的姓氏，你在申请中对做什么和不做什么都必须小心。

sentences.en: Don't attach a photograph.
sentences.zh: 不要附上照片。

sentences.en: Don't write an application essay about the importance of your family or the positive-negative aspects of living in two cultures,
sentences.zh: 不要写一篇关于家庭重要性或在两种文化中生活的好坏方面的申请论文，

sentences.en: something that most kids think is good to write about.
sentences.zh: 大多数孩子认为这些是很好的写作主题。

sentences.en: I mean, this is extraordinary advice that suggests that this is kind of a baked-in, understood phenomenon in higher education.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这是非同寻常的建议，表明这在高等教育中是一种根深蒂固、心照不宣的现象。

sentences.en: It does.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: It's the stereotyping that these kids are concerned about and that they think is unjustified.
sentences.zh: 这些孩子所关心并且认为不合理的就是这种刻板印象。

sentences.en: And how did this Harvard case come about in the first place?
sentences.zh: 哈佛案最初是怎么回事？

sentences.en: It was orchestrated by Edward Bloom.
sentences.zh: 这是由爱德华·布鲁姆策划的。

sentences.en: My name is Edward Bloom.
sentences.zh: 我的名字叫爱德华·布鲁姆。

sentences.en: He's a former stockbroker.
sentences.zh: 他是一名曾任证券经纪人的人。

sentences.en: He's not a lawyer.
sentences.zh: 他不是律师。

sentences.en: I have described myself as something like Yenta the matchmaker.
sentences.zh: 我曾将自己描述为类似媒婆延塔（Yenta）那样的人物。

sentences.en: He's filed a number of court cases.
sentences.zh: 他提起过许多法庭诉讼。

sentences.en: Two gigantic blockbuster cases.
sentences.zh: 两个轰动性的大案件。

sentences.en: Edward Bloom has a knack for finding the right plaintiff to get the justices' attention.
sentences.zh: 爱德华·布鲁姆有一种天赋，能找到合适的原告来吸引大法官们的注意。

sentences.en: We've seen him before and we'll see him again.
sentences.zh: 我们以前见过他，以后还会见到他。

sentences.en: He's become very adept at this.
sentences.zh: 他在这方面变得非常娴熟。

sentences.en: I confess I have a vanity plate and it is the address of the U.S.
sentences.zh: 我承认我有一个个性车牌，上面是美国

sentences.en: Supreme Court.
sentences.zh: 最高法院的地址。

sentences.en: And the mission is to see if I can get another case back there.
sentences.zh: 我的使命是看看能否把另一个案件带回那里。

sentences.en: So tell me how you got into this work because, of course, as you said, you're not a lawyer.
sentences.zh: 所以告诉我你是怎么开始从事这项工作的，因为正如你所说，你不是律师。

sentences.en: So what's the story there?
sentences.zh: 那背后的故事是什么？

sentences.en: That story begins with my wife and I living in a kind of a garden variety Houston neighborhood.
sentences.zh: 这个故事始于我和妻子住在休斯顿一个普普通通的居民区。

sentences.en: We decided that we wanted to move closer to the inner city, you know, a little trendier, a little hipper.
sentences.zh: 我们决定搬到离市中心更近的地方，你知道的，更时髦一点，更前卫一点。

sentences.en: So we did that.
sentences.zh: 所以我们照做了。

sentences.en: And when we went to vote for the first time in our new neighborhood, the Republican Party had not fielded a candidate.
sentences.zh: 当我们第一次在我们的新社区投票时，共和党没有派出候选人。

sentences.en: So I ended up running for Congress as the Republican nominee in that district.
sentences.zh: 所以我最终作为该选区的共和党候选人竞选国会议员。

sentences.en: My wife and I went door to door and introduced ourselves to the voters of the 18th Congressional District of Texas.
sentences.zh: 我和妻子挨家挨户向德克萨斯州第18国会选区的选民介绍自己。

sentences.en: It was during that process of determining who was in this congressional district,
sentences.zh: 正是在确定这个国会选区内都有谁的过程中，

sentences.en: we realized the Texas legislature had block by block identified residents by their race and ethnicity and harvested them into a congressional district.
sentences.zh: 我们意识到德克萨斯州立法机关按街区根据居民的种族和族裔对他们进行了识别，并将他们划分到一个国会选区中。

sentences.en: So you're describing what you believe to be a racially gerrymandered district.
sentences.zh: 所以你描述的是你认为存在种族不公划分选区的选区。

sentences.en: A racially gerrymandered district.
sentences.zh: 一个存在种族不公划分的选区。

sentences.en: I lost the race, but I sued the state of Texas.
sentences.zh: 我输了那场竞选，但我起诉了德克萨斯州。

sentences.en: First time I'd ever filed a lawsuit.
sentences.zh: 这是我第一次提起诉讼。

sentences.en: That was my first win at the Supreme Court.
sentences.zh: 那是我在最高法院的第一次胜利。

sentences.en: And that was the beginning of my legal advocacy in the arena of race and ethnicity.
sentences.zh: 那是我在种族和族裔领域法律维权的开始。

sentences.en: He's become very adept at this.
sentences.zh: 他在这方面变得非常熟练。

sentences.en: He orchestrated the Fisher v.
sentences.zh: 他策划了“费雪诉

sentences.en: University of Texas at Austin case, which went to the Supreme Court and was decided just last year.
sentences.zh: 德克萨斯大学奥斯汀分校案”，该案上诉至最高法院，并于去年做出裁决。

sentences.en: Abigail Fisher applied to the University of Texas in 2008.
sentences.zh: 阿比盖尔·费雪于2008年申请了德克萨斯大学。

sentences.en: Abby is a shy young woman, strawberry blonde, played the cello, and she was rejected from UT.
sentences.zh: 艾比是一个害羞的年轻女性，有着草莓金色的头发，拉大提琴，她被德克萨斯大学拒绝了。

sentences.en: What was the central question in her case, which got before the Supreme Court?
sentences.zh: 提交给最高法院的她的案件的核心问题是什么？

sentences.en: So that was an anti-white discrimination case.
sentences.zh: 所以那是一个反白人歧视案。

sentences.en: I hope the court rules that a student's race and ethnicity should not be considered when applying to the University of Texas.
sentences.zh: 我希望法院裁定，在申请德克萨斯大学时不应考虑学生的种族和族裔。

sentences.en: We have had a decision just handed down in what was billed as the landmark affirmative action case of this term.
sentences.zh: 我们刚刚对被称为本学期具有里程碑意义的平权法案做出了裁决。

sentences.en: The court ruled that universities may consider race in student admissions.
sentences.zh: 法院裁定，大学在招生时可以考虑种族因素。

sentences.en: Affirmative action in higher education is constitutional.
sentences.zh: 高等教育中的平权法案是合宪的。

sentences.en: In a 4-3 ruling handed down Thursday morning, a divided Supreme Court upheld racial preferences and university admissions.
sentences.zh: 在周四上午发布的4比3裁决中，意见分歧的最高法院维持了大学招生中的种族优待政策。

sentences.en: Justice Anthony Kennedy, writing for the majority,
sentences.zh: 大法官安东尼·肯尼迪代表多数派撰写意见书，

sentences.en: argued for American education's need to reconcile the pursuit of diversity with a constitutional promise of equal treatment and dignity.
sentences.zh: 论证了美国教育需要将追求多样性与宪法对平等对待和尊严的承诺调和起来。

sentences.en: A painful day, I think, for all of us who labor for the elimination of race in higher education.
sentences.zh: 我认为，对所有为消除高等教育中的种族因素而努力的人来说，这是痛苦的一天。

sentences.en: One of the dissenting justices, Alito, did mention Asian Americans as a troubling example of how affirmative action might do something wrong.
sentences.zh: 持不同意见的大法官之一阿利托确实提到了亚裔美国人，这是一个令人不安的例子，说明平权法案可能会做错事。

sentences.en: At that time, I remember talking to Lee Bollinger, who's now head of Columbia University,
sentences.zh: 当时，我记得跟现在担任哥伦比亚大学校长的李·博林格交谈过，

sentences.en: was at the University of Michigan Law School when it was the target of an affirmative action lawsuit.
sentences.zh: 他当时在密歇根大学法学院，当时该学院是平权法案诉讼的目标。

sentences.en: And he said, just wait and see.
sentences.zh: 他说，咱们走着瞧。

sentences.en: Asian Americans are going to be next.
sentences.zh: 亚裔美国人将是下一个。

sentences.en: You know, that's the way that the anti-affirmative action people are going to go.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这就是那些反对平权行动的人会走的路。

sentences.en: And that's exactly what we did.
sentences.zh: 而这正是我们所做的。

sentences.en: In November of 2014, we sued Harvard University, arguing that Harvard has a quota that limits the number of Asians it will accept,
sentences.zh: 在2014年11月，我们起诉了哈佛大学，辩称哈佛大学设有名额限制，限制了其录取的亚裔人数，

sentences.en: much like Harvard's quota on Jews during the 1920s, 30s, and 40s.
sentences.zh: 这很像20世纪20年代、30年代和40年代哈佛对犹太人的名额限制。

sentences.en: Did you go out and specifically recruit Asian plaintiffs?
sentences.zh: 你们有没有特意去找亚裔原告？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I had to make a lot of phone calls.
sentences.zh: 我不得不打了许多电话。

sentences.en: I had to launch a website called harvardnotfair.org.
sentences.zh: 我不得不建立一个名为harvardnotfair.org的网站。

sentences.en: Harvardnotfair.org.
sentences.zh: Harvardnotfair.org.

sentences.en: Let me actually type that into the browser here.
sentences.zh: 让我在这里把它输入浏览器。

sentences.en: So what I see is a photo of a dejected-looking Asian woman, and the banner next to her says, Were you denied admission to Harvard?
sentences.zh: 我看到的是一张面容沮丧的亚裔女性的照片，她旁边的横幅上写着：你被哈佛拒绝录取了吗？

sentences.en: It may be because you're the wrong race.
sentences.zh: 这可能是因为你的种族不对。

sentences.en: That is the basis of that lawsuit.
sentences.zh: 这就是这起诉讼的基础。

sentences.en: Asians are an important part of the Ivy League, and our belief is that they are the ones that are racial preferences than really any other race.
sentences.zh: 亚裔是常春藤盟校的重要组成部分，而我们的信念是，与其他任何种族相比，他们才是真正受到种族照顾的人。

sentences.en: So looking back at the kind of chronology and order of these lawsuits, from the outside, it looks like you and your role as a kind of legal yenta, as you've described it,
sentences.zh: 因此，回看这些诉讼的时间线和顺序，从局外人的角度来看，就像你和你所描述的法律老娘舅角色一样，

sentences.en: went to the Supreme Court with a white plaintiff in the affirmative action case in Texas and lost that case, and then went and sought to find an Asian student in the Harvard case.
sentences.zh: 在德克萨斯州的平权行动案中带着一位白人原告去了最高法院并输掉了官司，然后又去哈佛案中寻找一名亚裔学生。

sentences.en: Why did you make that turn?
sentences.zh: 你为什么要做出这样的转变？

sentences.en: It's not like we abandon representing white kids.
sentences.zh: 这并不是说我们放弃了代表白人孩子。

sentences.en: It's just that's the group that is most harmed by Harvard's quota system.
sentences.zh: 只是那是受哈佛配额制伤害最深的群体。

sentences.en: So why do you do this work, Edward?
sentences.zh: 爱德华，你为什么要这样做？

sentences.en: Why have you devoted so much of your life now to trying to dismantle these race-based protections?
sentences.zh: 你为什么现在把这么多的生命奉献于试图废除这些基于种族的保护措施？

sentences.en: That's a good question, and I don't know that I have a good answer.
sentences.zh: 这是一个好问题，我不知道我有没有一个好答案。

sentences.en: I guess this was just something that I grew up with, the lessons that my mother and father, and frankly, maybe liberal Judaism taught me,
sentences.zh: 我想这只是我从小接触的事物，我的父母，坦白说，也许还有自由派犹太教教给我的道理，

sentences.en: that the foundation of civil rights is that your race and your ethnicity should not be something that's used to help you, nor should it be used to harm you.
sentences.zh: 民权的基石在于，你的种族和族裔不应该成为帮助你的工具，也不应该成为伤害你的工具。

sentences.en: And all that I'm trying to do is to restore that original civil rights vision.
sentences.zh: 而我所试图做的一切，就是恢复最初的民权愿景。

sentences.en: I guess that's why I do it.
sentences.zh: 我想这就是我这样做的原因。

sentences.en: So looking at the history of your lawsuits and what they're aimed at, they pursue many of the biggest accomplishments in the civil rights movement, voting rights,
sentences.zh: 因此，看看你的诉讼历史及其目标，它们追求的是民权运动中许多最大的成就，投票权，

sentences.en: affirmative action.
sentences.zh: 平权行动。

sentences.en: What do you say to those who conclude that your goal is to basically undo the advances of the civil rights movement?
sentences.zh: 对于那些得出结论认为你的目标基本上是抹杀民权运动成果的人，你想对他们说些什么？

sentences.en: Well, it's a false question, to be frank.
sentences.zh: 嗯，坦白说，这是一个伪命题。

sentences.en: It is, I'm not trying to undo the advancements.
sentences.zh: 确实如此，我并不是想抹杀这些成果。

sentences.en: I'm trying to restore the original vision, but you cannot cure past racial discrimination with new racial discrimination.
sentences.zh: 我正试图恢复最初的愿景，但你不能用新的种族歧视来治愈过去的种族歧视。

sentences.en: That's the bottom line.
sentences.zh: 这就是底线。

sentences.en: So finally, I want to ask you about the interest of our president in this issue.
sentences.zh: 最后，我想问你关于我们总统对这个问题的兴趣。

sentences.en: What did you think when you heard that President Trump has called for lawyers inside the Department of Justice to investigate race-based admissions and the possibility of discrimination in those admissions policies?
sentences.zh: 当你听到特朗普总统呼吁司法部内部的律师调查基于种族的招生以及这些招生政策中存在歧视的可能性时，你有什么想法？

sentences.en: Any administration fully at this issue hold these universities' feet to the fire and make sure that they are complying with Supreme Court jurisprudence in this.
sentences.zh: 任何政府如果全力关注这一问题，就要让这些大学承担责任，并确保它们在这方面遵守最高法院的判例。

sentences.en: I applaud that.
sentences.zh: 我对此表示赞赏。

sentences.en: America applauds that.
sentences.zh: 美国赞赏这一点。

sentences.en: And I hope to see more of it.
sentences.zh: 我希望看到更多这样的举措。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: Nicole Hannah-Jones covers race and education for The Times.
sentences.zh: 妮可·汉娜-琼斯为《时报》报道种族与教育问题。

sentences.en: I interviewed Edward Bloom, and he will readily admit that we have a fundamentally unequal and segregated K-12 system,
sentences.zh: 我采访了爱德华·布鲁姆，他会欣然承认我们拥有一个根本上不平等且呈隔离状态的K-12教育系统，

sentences.en: but then would like to pretend that once we get to college admissions, we are a meritocracy.
sentences.zh: 但随后又想假装一旦到了大学招生阶段，我们就成了一个精英统治社会。

sentences.en: And every child, every student should be treated as if they came from the same place.
sentences.zh: 每个孩子、每个学生都应该被当作来自同一个地方来对待。

sentences.en: So given the scope of Edward Bloom's work and what you know about him, both from his track record with lawsuits and from your conversations with him,
sentences.zh: 因此，鉴于爱德华·布鲁姆的工作范围以及你对他了解的情况，无论是从他打官司的记录来看，还是从你与他的对话来看，

sentences.en: do you believe that this lawsuit that he helped file against Harvard is about discrimination against Asian Americans?
sentences.zh: 你认为他协助对哈佛发起的这场诉讼是关于针对亚裔美国人的歧视吗？

sentences.en: Or is it about something else?
sentences.zh: 还是说关乎其他什么？

sentences.en: I think that Edward Bloom is using Asian Americans the way that many white Americans have used Asian Americans since the myth of the model minority began.
sentences.zh: 我认为爱德华·布鲁姆正在利用亚裔美国人，就像自从模范少数族裔神话出现以来，许多白人美国人利用亚裔美国人的方式一样。

sentences.en: The myth of the model minority starts to come about in the 1960s, and it's a direct reaction to the push for civil rights of black Americans.
sentences.zh: 模范少数族裔的神话开始于20世纪60年代，它是对黑人美国人争取民权诉求的直接反应。

sentences.en: And what it says is it begins to hold up Asian Americans as a group of people who are a racial minority who came to this country and worked hard and were able to succeed.
sentences.zh: 它的核心表述是，开始将亚裔美国人树立为一个作为一个种族少数群体的群体，他们来到这个国家并努力工作，从而取得了成功。

sentences.en: And in that case, you were able to use Asian Americans to show that America really doesn't have a race problem.
sentences.zh: 在这种情况下，你能够利用亚裔美国人来证明美国其实没有种族问题。

sentences.en: It's black people who have the problem.
sentences.zh: 有问题的黑人。

sentences.en: So they become a foil.
sentences.zh: 所以他们成了一个衬托。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So the current lawsuit is just the most current iteration of that, which is to say black Americans,
sentences.zh: 因此，当前的诉讼只是这一现象的最新翻版，也就是说，黑人美国人、

sentences.en: Latinos are complaining that they need help to get into college because of an unfair system.
sentences.zh: 拉丁裔正在抱怨他们需要帮助才能进入大学，因为这是一个不公平的系统。

sentences.en: Well, look at this minority group over here.
sentences.zh: 瞧瞧这边这个少数族裔群体。

sentences.en: If we were really an unfair, racist country, how could Asian Americans be doing so well?
sentences.zh: 如果我们真的是一个不公平、种族主义的国家，亚裔美国人怎么可能过得这么好？

sentences.en: So how did we arrive at the affirmative action system in the first place?
sentences.zh: 那么我们当初是如何建立平权行动制度的呢？

sentences.en: What did it set out to do?
sentences.zh: 它原本的目标是什么？

sentences.en: If we understand the roots of affirmative action, Linda B.
sentences.zh: 如果我们理解平权行动的根源，林德·B·

sentences.en: Johnson is the first politician who talks about affirmative action in a 1965 speech.
sentences.zh: 约翰逊是第一位在1965年的一次演讲中谈到平权行动的政治家。

sentences.en: You do not take a person who for years has been hobbled by chains and liberating,
sentences.zh: 你不能把一个多年来一直被锁链束缚、步履维艰的人，

sentences.en: bringing up to the starting line of a race and then say you are free to compete with all the others.
sentences.zh: 拉到赛跑的起跑线上，然后说你现在可以自由地与其他人竞争了。

sentences.en: And still justly believe that you have been completely fair.
sentences.zh: 并且仍然理直气壮地认为你是绝对公平的。

sentences.en: It is not saying that they didn't work hard or they're not qualified.
sentences.zh: 这并不是说他们没有努力工作或者他们不够优秀。

sentences.en: It's saying that they have not had the same advantages.
sentences.zh: 这是在说他们没有获得相同的优势。

sentences.en: By the school you go to and the poverty or the richness of your surroundings.
sentences.zh: 通过你所上的学校以及你周围环境的贫困或富裕程度。

sentences.en: When we think about college admissions, I think what often gets lost is colleges are looking at a bunch of different things at all times to determine who they're going to accept.
sentences.zh: 当我们思考大学招生时，我认为经常被忽视的是，大学在任何时候都在考察一系列不同的事情，以决定录取谁。

sentences.en: Colleges admit students because they want geographic diversity.
sentences.zh: 大学录取学生是因为他们想要地域多样性。

sentences.en: White women outscore white men on test scores, but colleges want gender balance.
sentences.zh: 白人女性的考试成绩高于白人男性，但大学希望保持性别平衡。

sentences.en: It is only when it comes to race that we have a problem, even though black students are only 5% of all students enrolled at flagship universities.
sentences.zh: 只有在涉及种族问题时我们才有麻烦，尽管黑人学生仅占旗舰大学所有注册学生的5%。

sentences.en: So even with so-called affirmative action,
sentences.zh: 因此，即使有了所谓的平权行动，

sentences.en: you cannot argue that black students are taking the slots of white students because they are still underrepresented at any of the flagship universities.
sentences.zh: 你也不能争辩说黑人学生抢占了白人的名额，因为他们在任何旗舰大学中仍然代表性不足。

sentences.en: So with all that in mind, is affirmative action doing what it set out to do, especially in college admissions now?
sentences.zh: 因此，考虑到这一切，平权行动是否在做它原定要做的事情，尤其是在现在的大学招生中？

sentences.en: I mean, no.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，没有。

sentences.en: I think, again,
sentences.zh: 我认为，再次说明，

sentences.en: the fact that only 5% of the students at flagship universities are black students with affirmative action shows that it actually hasn't done a great job of catching students up.
sentences.zh: 旗舰大学中黑人学生仅占5%这一事实表明，借助平权行动，它实际上在帮助学生迎头赶上方面并没有做得很好。

sentences.en: It is not opening the opportunities for black students to get into the best universities.
sentences.zh: 它并没有为黑人学生进入最好的大学创造机会。

sentences.en: And in fact, what we do know is that white women have been the greatest benefactors of affirmative action because in order to get affirmative action policies passed,
sentences.zh: 事实上，我们所知道的是，白人女性一直是平权行动最大的受益者，因为为了让平权行动政策得以通过，

sentences.en: they had to include white women as a historically oppressed minority group.
sentences.zh: 他们不得不把白人女性作为一个历史上受压迫的少数群体包容进来。

sentences.en: That was what more conservative people forced into legislation and policy in order to pass affirmative action.
sentences.zh: 为了通过平权行动，更保守的人士将这一点强行塞入了立法和政策中。

sentences.en: So if you look at white women's college attendance, when you look at white women's earning capacity and entry into kind of the corporate world,
sentences.zh: 因此，如果你看看白人女性的大学入学率，看看白人女性的创收能力和进入公司世界的状况，

sentences.en: their numbers far outnumber black Americans.
sentences.zh: 她们的人数远超黑人美国人。

sentences.en: Though people don't tend to think of them as beneficiaries of affirmative action, they certainly are.
sentences.zh: 尽管人们往往不认为她们是平权行动的受益者，但她们绝对是。

sentences.en: With that said, in states that have eliminated affirmative action altogether, you've seen a significant drop in enrollment of black and Latino students.
sentences.zh: 话虽如此，在完全取消了平权行动的州，黑人和拉丁裔学生的入学人数出现了显著下降。

sentences.en: So what we have isn't great, but if we don't have it, it's going to be a lot worse.
sentences.zh: 所以我们拥有的制度并不完美，但如果我们没有它，情况会糟糕得多。

sentences.en: Here is what else you need to know today.
sentences.zh: 以下是你今天还需要了解的其他内容。

sentences.en: Transcripts leaked to The Washington Post reveal the details of tense conversations between President Trump and two foreign leaders during Trump's early days in office.
sentences.zh: 泄露给《华盛顿邮报》的通话记录揭示了特朗普总统在任职初期与两位外国领导人之间紧张对话的细节。

sentences.en: Talking to Mexican President Enrique Peña Nieto, Trump said,
sentences.zh: 在与墨西哥总统恩里克·培尼亚·涅托交谈时，特朗普说：

sentences.en: If you are going to say that Mexico is not going to pay for the wall, then I do not want to meet with you guys anymore because I cannot live with that.
sentences.zh: 如果你要说墨西哥不会为这堵墙付钱，那么我不想再和你们见面了，因为我无法忍受这一点。

sentences.en: The call with Australian Prime Minister Malcolm Turnbull was even more contentious.
sentences.zh: 与澳大利亚总理马尔科姆·特恩布尔的通话则更具争端性。

sentences.en: With Trump calling an agreement with President Obama to consider accepting 1,250 economic refugees.
sentences.zh: 特朗普称与奥巴马总统达成的一项考虑接受1250名经济难民的协议

sentences.en: Quote, a disgusting deal.
sentences.zh: 原话是：一个令人作呕的协议。

sentences.en: I have had it, the president said towards the end of the call.
sentences.zh: 我受够了，总统在通话快结束时说道。

sentences.en: I have been making these calls all day, and this is the most unpleasant call all day.
sentences.zh: 我一整天都在打这些电话，这是我一整天最不愉快的通话。

sentences.en: Putin was a pleasant call.
sentences.zh: 普京那通电话挺愉快的。

sentences.en: This is ridiculous.
sentences.zh: 这太荒谬了。

sentences.en: Today I will tell you with lots of prayers and lots of thinking, today I will tell you as West Virginians, I can't help you anymore being a Democrat governor.
sentences.zh: 今天我要告诉你们，经过大量的祈祷和深思熟虑，今天我要以西弗吉尼亚州人的身份告诉你们，我不能再以民主党州长的身份帮助你们了。

sentences.en: At a Trump rally in West Virginia on Thursday night, with the president by his side, the newly elected Democratic governor of West Virginia announced that he is switching parties.
sentences.zh: 周四晚上，在西弗吉尼亚州的一场特朗普集会上，在总统的陪同下，新当选的西弗吉尼亚州民主党州长宣布他将转换党派。

sentences.en: So tomorrow, I will be changing my registration to Republican.
sentences.zh: 所以明天，我将把我的党籍登记更改为共和党。

sentences.en: In doing so, Jim Justice, a billionaire coal and real estate magnate, becomes the first sitting Democratic governor to switch parties in 25 years.
sentences.zh: 通过这样做，身家亿万的煤炭和房地产大亨吉姆·贾斯蒂斯成为了25年来第一位转换党派的现任民主党州长。

sentences.en: I want to thank your great governor.
sentences.zh: 我要感谢你们伟大的州长。

sentences.en: Having Big Jim as a Republican is such an honor, I will tell you.
sentences.zh: 拥有大吉姆作为一名共和党人是如此的荣幸，我得告诉你们。

sentences.en: Such an honor.
sentences.zh: 真是莫大的荣幸。

sentences.zh: 《每日新闻》由西奥·巴尔科姆、林赛·加里森、雷切尔·克斯特、安妮·布朗、安迪·米尔斯和克里斯托弗·沃思制作。

sentences.zh: 丽莎·托宾是我们的执行制作人。

sentences.zh: 萨曼莎·亨尼格是我们的编辑总监。

sentences.zh: 我们的主题音乐由Wonderly的吉姆·布伦伯格和本·兰斯伯格创作。

sentences.zh: 以上就是本期《每日新闻》的全部内容。

sentences.en: I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是迈克尔·巴尔巴罗。

sentences.en: See you Monday.
sentences.zh: 周一见。

sentences.en: For decades, the Brooklyn Democratic Party operated as a tightly controlled machine.
sentences.zh: 几十年来，布鲁克林民主党一直像一个受到严密控制的机器一样运作。

sentences.en: Until this summer.
sentences.zh: 直到今年夏天。

sentences.en: When elections ushered in a bunch of self-described reformers.
sentences.zh: 当时选举迎来了自称改革派的一群人。
